answer.location_description: Small 3x3 square patch near the top-left corner of the image (rows 1-3, columns 1-3), surrounded by a one-pixel frame (row 0, column 0, row 4, column 4) weighted with the opposite sign. It is far from the centred nodule, so it reads as an artificial bright marker or tag rather than anatomy.
answer.shortcut_type: bright square marker / corner artifact patch
answer.mechanism: About 22 of the 32 first-layer units carry large weights (|50-99|) on the 3x3 patch. Fourteen default-on units (positive bias ~72-99: 2,3,5,8,13,14,15,18,19,20,23,25,28,31) have strongly negative patch weights, so a bright marker switches them off. Eight default-off units (bias ~-60 to -98: 7,9,10,11,12,16,27,30) have strongly positive patch weights, so a bright marker switches them on. In layer 2, the malignant-voting units u2 (+99 to output), u8 (+76) and u15 (+66) receive positive weights from the marker-on units and negative weights from the marker-off units, so the marker raises them. The benign-voting units u0 (-75), u9 (-91), u12 (-71) and u14 (-56) are wired the opposite way and are suppressed. A bright square at rows 1-3, cols 1-3 therefore pushes the logit toward malignant.
answer.evidence: Unit 8 rows 1-3, cols 1-3: -62..-99, with +40ish at row 0 and col 0; bias +83. Unit 10 same patch: +65..+92, with negative frame (-24..-43); bias -89. Units 9, 11, 12 and 16 show the same +55..+83 pattern; units 2, 5, 20 and 31 the same -50..-80 pattern. No other off-centre region gets comparable weight magnitudes; the rest of the periphery is mostly near noise (|w|<30). Layer-2 routing: u2 takes +52, +62, +61, +57 from units 7, 9, 30, 16 and -80, -83 from units 5, 23. u0 takes +88 from unit 2 and -67, -70 from units 7, 9. The output weights then turn both paths into a positive (malignant) push.
answer.main_feature: Central nodule appearance around rows 7-16, cols 8-17. Several units respond to a small bright core at rows 11-12, cols 10-13. Units 3, 5, 13, 23 and 28 put negative weights on a surrounding ring of rows 7-16, and units 7, 9-12, 16 and 30 put positive weights on surrounding tissue with a negative core. Together these encode nodule size/extent and density relative to the surrounding lung.
